spots.name: Cathedral of St. John the Baptist

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Basilica of St. John the Baptist is a Roman Catholic cathedral and minor basilica near Lafayette Square at 222 East Harris Street, Savannah, Georgia, in the United States. It is the mother church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Savannah.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral Basilica of St. John the Baptist (Savannah, Georgia)

spots.name: Bonaventure Cemetery
spots.summary: Bonaventure Cemetery is a rural cemetery located on a scenic bluff of the Wilmington River, southeast of downtown Savannah, Georgia.

spots.name: Congregation Mickve Israel

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Congregation Mickve Israel is a Reform Jewish congregation and synagogue located at 20 East Gordon Street, Monterey Square, in Savannah, Georgia, in the United States. The site also contains a Jewish history museum.

spots.name: Savannah Victorian Historic District
spots.summary: The Savannah Victorian Historic District is a historic district in Savannah, Georgia. It is mostly residential in character and features Late Victorian, Queen Anne, and other architectural styles.

spots.name: Savannah Historic District
spots.summary: The Savannah Historic District is a large urban U.S. historic district that roughly corresponds to the pre–Civil War city limits of Savannah, Georgia. The area was declared a National Historic Landmark District in 1966, and is one of the largest urban, community-wide historic preservation districts in the United States.

spots.name: Mercer House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Mercer House is an Italianate mansion at 429 Bull Street in Savannah, Georgia, United States. Completed in 1868, it occupies the southwestern civic block of Monterey Square in the city's Historic District.

photo.author: Kyle Kesselring from Canal Winchester, OH

spots.name: Sorrel–Weed House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old Sorrel–Weed House Museum, or the Francis Sorrel House, is a historic landmark in Savannah, Georgia located at 6 West Harris Street in Savannah, Georgia.

spots.name: Colonial Park Cemetery
spots.summary: Colonial Park Cemetery is an 18th- and early 19th-century burial ground located in downtown Savannah, Georgia. It became a city park in 1896, 43 years after burials in the cemetery ceased, and is open to visitors.

spots.name: Forsyth Park
spots.summary: Forsyth Park is a large city park that occupies 30 acres (0.12 km2) in the Savannah Historic District of Savannah, Georgia, United States. The park is bordered by Gaston Street to the north, Drayton Street to the east, Park Avenue to the south and Whitaker Street to the west.

spots.name: Georgia State Railroad Museum
spots.summary: The Georgia State Railroad Museum is a museum in Savannah, Georgia, located at a historic Central of Georgia Railway site. It includes parts of the Central of Georgia Railway: Savannah Shops and Terminal Facilities National Historic Landmark District.

spots.name: Green–Meldrim House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Green–Meldrim House is a historic house at 14 West Macon Street, on the northwest corner of Madison Square, in Savannah, Georgia. Built in 1853, it was designated as a National Historic Landmark in 1976 as one of the American South's finest and most lavish examples of Gothic Revival architecture.

spots.name: Chippewa Square
spots.summary: Chippewa Square is one of the 22 squares of Savannah, Georgia, United States. It is located in the middle row of the city's five rows of squares, on Bull Street and McDonough Street, and was laid out in 1815.

spots.name: First African Baptist Church

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: First African Baptist Church, located in Savannah, Georgia, claims to be derived from the first black Baptist congregation in North America. While it was not officially organized until 1788, it grew from members who founded a congregation in 1773.

spots.name: James Oglethorpe Monument
spots.summary: The James Oglethorpe Monument is a public monument in Chippewa Square, Savannah, Georgia, United States. It honors James Oglethorpe, the founder of the Province of Georgia, who established the city of Savannah in 1733.

spots.name: Savannah station
spots.summary: Savannah station is a former passenger depot and trainshed constructed in 1860 by the Central of Georgia Railway (CofG) before the outbreak of the American Civil War.

spots.name: Christ Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Christ Church is an Episcopal church at 28 Bull Street, Johnson Square, in Savannah, Georgia. Founded in 1733, it was the first church established in the Province of Georgia and one of the first parishes within the Episcopal Diocese of Georgia, earning it the nickname "the Mother Church of Georgia".

spots.name: Casimir Pulaski Monument
spots.summary: The Casimir Pulaski Monument in Savannah, or Pulaski Monument on Monterey Square, is a 19th-century monument to Casimir Pulaski, in Monterey Square, on Bull Street, Savannah, Georgia, not far from the battlefield where Pulaski lost his life during the siege of Savannah.

spots.name: Monterey Square
spots.summary: Monterey Square is one of the 22 squares of Savannah, Georgia, United States. It is located in the southernmost row of the city's five rows of squares, on Bull Street and Wayne Street, and was laid out in 1847. It is south of Madison Square, west of Taylor Square, north of Forsyth Park and east of Chatham Square.

spots.name: Flannery O'Connor Childhood Home

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Flannery O'Connor Childhood Home is a historic house museum in Savannah, Georgia where American author Flannery O'Connor lived during her childhood. The home, built in 1856, is located at 207 E. Charlton Street in Lafayette Square.

spots.name: Telfair Academy
spots.summary: The Telfair Academy is a historic mansion at 121 Barnard Street in Savannah, Georgia. It was designed by William Jay and built in 1818, and is one of a small number of Jay's surviving works. It is one of three sites owned by Telfair Museums.

spots.name: Nathanael Greene Monument
spots.summary: The Nathanael Greene Monument is a public monument in Savannah, Georgia, United States. Located in Johnson Square, the monument was designed by William Strickland and honors Nathanael Greene, a general in the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War.

spots.name: Jones Street
spots.summary: Jones Street is a historic street in Savannah, Georgia, United States. It is named for major John Jones, aide-de-camp to brigadier general Lachlan McIntosh at the 1779 siege of Savannah during the American Revolutionary War.

spots.name: Owens–Thomas House
spots.summary: The Owens–Thomas House & Slave Quarters is a historic home in Savannah, Georgia, that is operated as a historic house museum by Telfair Museums. It is located at 124 Abercorn Street, on the northeast corner of Oglethorpe Square.

spots.name: Juliette Gordon Low Historic District

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Juliette Gordon Low Historic District consists of three buildings in Savannah, Georgia, United States, which are associated with the origins of the Girl Scouts of the USA.

spots.name: Johnson Square
spots.summary: Johnson Square is one of the squares of Savannah, Georgia, United States. Located in the northernmost row of the city's five rows of squares, it was the first of the squares to be laid out, in 1733, and remains the largest of the 22 squares. It is east of Ellis Square, west of Reynolds Square and north of Wright Square.

spots.name: Savannah City Hall
spots.summary: Savannah City Hall is the seat of government for the city of Savannah, Georgia, United States. Designed by architect Hyman Witcover, the building was built between 1904 and 1905 and opened the following year. It is a contributing property to the Savannah Historic District.

spots.name: Telfair Museums

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Telfair Museums, in the historic district of Savannah, Georgia, was the first public art museum in the Southern United States.

spots.name: Andrew Low House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Andrew Low House is a home in Savannah, Georgia, United States. Located at 329 Abercorn Street, in Lafayette Square, it was built by John S. Norris in 1849 and is part of the Savannah Historic District and of the Juliette Gordon Low Historic District. It is the oldest building on Lafayette Square.

spots.name: William Scarbrough House
spots.summary: William Scarbrough House is a historic house in Savannah, Georgia. Built in 1819, and subjected to a number later alterations, it is nationally significant as an early example of Greek Revival architecture, and is one of the few surviving American works of architect William Jay.

spots.name: Civil War Memorial
spots.summary: The Civil War Memorial in Savannah, Georgia, is a monument honoring soldiers who died during the American Civil War. Located in Forsyth Park, it consists of a 48-foot (15 m) tall shaft topped with a bronze statue of a Confederate soldier.

spots.name: Independent Presbyterian Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Independent Presbyterian Church of Savannah, on Bull Street in Savannah, Georgia, is the first Presbyterian church in Georgia, founded in 1755. Land for its first building was deeded by King George II of Great Britain for use by colonial adherents of the Church of Scotland.

spots.name: Ellis Square
spots.summary: Ellis Square is one of the 22 squares of Savannah, Georgia, United States. It is located in the northernmost row of the city's five rows of squares, on Barnard Street and West St. Julian Street, and was one of the first four squares laid out. Today, it marks the western end of City Market.

spots.name: Davenport House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Isaiah Davenport House is a historic home in Savannah, Georgia, United States. Built in 1820, it has been operated as a historic house museum by the Historic Savannah Foundation since 1963.

spots.name: African-American Monument
spots.summary: The African-American Monument is a public monument in Savannah, Georgia, United States, dedicated in 2002. Located near River Street along the city's waterfront with the Savannah River, the monument commemorates African Americans in the city and highlights the "invisible story of the Trans Atlantic slave trade".

spots.name: William Jasper Monument
spots.summary: The William Jasper Monument is a monument honoring William Jasper in Savannah, Georgia, United States. Located in Madison Square, the monument was designed by Alexander Doyle and dedicated in 1888.

spots.name: Madison Square
spots.summary: Madison Square is one of the 22 squares of Savannah, Georgia, United States. It is located in the fourth row of the city's five rows of squares, on Bull Street and Macon Street, and was laid out in 1837. It is south of Chippewa Square, west of Lafayette Square, north of Monterey Square and east of Pulaski Square.

spots.name: First Bryan Baptist Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: First Bryan Baptist Church is a church organized in Savannah, Georgia by Andrew Bryan in 1788 for African-Americans. Considered to be the Mother Church of Black Baptists, the site was purchased in 1793 by Bryan, a former slave who had also purchased his freedom. The first structure was erected there in 1794.

spots.name: Oglethorpe Square
spots.summary: Oglethorpe Square is one of the 22 squares of Savannah, Georgia, United States. It is located in the second row of the city's five rows of squares, on Abercorn Street and East President Street, and was laid out in 1742.

spots.name: Lutheran Church of the Ascension

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Lutheran Church of the Ascension is a historic Lutheran church on Bull Street in Savannah, Georgia, located in the Savannah Historic District. The congregation was founded by Johann Martin Boltzius in 1741, with the current building constructed in 1843.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Lutheran Church of the Ascension (Savannah, Georgia)

spots.name: Wesley Monumental United Methodist Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wesley Monumental United Methodist Church is a Methodist church in Savannah, Georgia, United States. Located in Taylor Square, at 429 Abercorn Street, the building's first floor was completed in 1875, with the second floor added in 1878. The church was completed in 1890. Its spire and stucco were added five years later.

spots.name: Carver Village Historic District
spots.summary: The Carver Village Historic District is a historic district in Savannah, Georgia. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2019.

spots.name: Lucas Theatre
spots.summary: The Lucas Theatre is a theater on Abercorn Street in Reynolds Square, Savannah, Georgia, United States. Built in 1921, the theater closed in 1976 and was slated to be demolished, but preservation efforts led to it reopening in 2000.

spots.name: Hurn Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hurn Museum is a museum on Monterey Square in Savannah, Georgia, United States, devoted to American folk art, as well as the work of international self-taught artists. The museum is named after the late Deborah Hurn, a local champion of folk art in Savannah.

spots.name: Central of Georgia Railroad: Savannah Shops and Terminal Facilities
spots.summary: The Georgia State Railroad Museum is a museum in Savannah, Georgia, located at a historic Central of Georgia Railway site. It includes parts of the Central of Georgia Railway: Savannah Shops and Terminal Facilities National Historic Landmark District.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Central of Georgia Railroad: Savannah Shops and Terminal Facilities

spots.name: Central of Georgia Railway Company Shop Property
spots.summary: Central of Georgia Railway Company Shop Property is the former administration building of the Central of Georgia Railway.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Central of Georgia Railway Company Shop Property

spots.name: City Market

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: City Market is a mixed-use project in the northwest corner of the Historic District. The rehabilitation of the four-block area began in 1985. The result is a facility that economically could not be replicated today. City Market has established itself as a destination for entertainment, dining, and retailing in downtown Savannah.
